newsitem.title: ITALY: Rolo Banca aims for ROE of 17 pct in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Rolo Banca aims for ROE of 17 pct in 1999.

text.p: Italian banking group Rolo Banca is aiming to reach a return of equity of 17 percent by the end of 1999, in what the bank describes as an "ambitious objective but realisable".

The heads of the banking group, in which Credito Italiano has a controlling stake, told a press conference on Thursday this would be acheived by a rise in volume, structural rationalisation and greater synergies with Credito.
In 1996, the group's return on equity doubled to 12 percent from six percent in 1995 and will rise steadily over the next three years, said the group's director general Cesare Farsetti.
For 1997 the bank was progressing well, in line with its own budget with a very small margin increase. The bank added that for the moment it did not foresee any acquisitions.

The bank showed a net profit of 408 billion lire in 1996, up 144 percent, while the ROE ratio of 12 percent in 1996 was already ahead of the 11 percent originally forecast for 1998. The ratio of bad loans to total loans is expected to fall to 2.9 percent by 1999 from 4.3 percent seen in 1996.
One of the hinges of the group's development will be the increase in managed funds which rose by four trillion lire from the 15 trillion lire at the end of 1996, the bank said.
